title: Components: The Basics
summary: The building block of every Angular app — a reusable piece of UI.
heading: Components: The Basics

blocks.text: A component is one reusable piece of the screen — a header, a button, a card, a whole page. An Angular app is really just a tree of components nested inside each other.

blocks.caption: An app is a tree of components.

blocks.text: A component is a class (Chapter 8) with a @Component label on top. The label tells Angular three things: the tag name to use it as, where its template is, and where its styles are.

blocks.label: hello.ts

layers.title: selector
layers.detail: The custom tag you write to use the component

layers.title: styles
layers.detail: CSS that applies only to this component

layers.title: class
layers.detail: The data and logic behind it

blocks.text: Once a component has a selector, you use it like an HTML tag inside another component's template. First make it available by adding it to imports.

blocks.label: app.ts

blocks.text: Modern Angular components are standalone — each one lists its own imports, so there are no big NgModules to manage.
Here's a component you can edit and run — the class holds the data, the template shows it:

blocks.ts:
title = 'My First Component';
tagline = 'Reusable piece of UI';

blocks.text: You don't write all those files by hand. The CLI generates a component — class, template, and styles — and wires the naming for you.

blocks.label: Terminal
blocks.code:
ng generate component hello
# short version:
ng g c hello

items: A component is a reusable piece of UI; an app is a tree of them.
It's a class with a @Component label.
The label sets the selector, template, and styles.
Use a component by its selector tag, after adding it to imports.
Generate one with ng g c name.
